item.text: {"search_note":"I did not find strong 2024 evidence that Hasina personally made equal opportunity a governing priority across the state. The clearest positives are mostly humanitarian, technocratic, or partner-led. I also did not find convincing evidence of broad, consistent anti-discrimination reform that would offset the stronger reports of punitive camp policy, unequal access, and repression.","evidence":[{"title":"Bangladesh - Cash Transfer Modernization Project : Improving Transparency and Efficiency of Safety Nets","publisher":"World Bank","date":"January 1, 2024","url":"https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099739201032424234","summary":"Bangladesh already had cash transfers for old-age, widow/destitute women, and disability programs; the modernization project aimed to improve targeting, administration, and benefit payments. This is limited evidence of needs-based distribution rather than loyalty punishment.","question_ids":["6B.8","6B.7"]},{"title":"UN and partners seek $852.4m support Rohingya refugees and Bangladeshi hosts","publisher":"UNHCR / UN in Bangladesh","date":"March 13, 2024","url":"https://www.unhcr.org/news/press-releases/un-and-partners-seek-852-4m-support-rohingya-refugees-and-bangladeshi-hosts","summary":"The 2024 Rohingya plan under Bangladeshi authorities targeted food, shelter, health care, protection, education, and livelihoods for refugees and host communities, especially women and children. That is a genuine dignity/equal-access signal, though it is humanitarian coordination rather than proof of Hasina personally broadening equality.","question_ids":["6B.8","6B.6","6B.7"]},{"title":"World Bank helps Bangladesh provide basic services, opportunities and build resilience for displaced Rohingya and host communities","publisher":"World Bank","date":"May 28, 2024","url":"https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/05/28/world-bank-helps-bangladesh-provide-basic-services-opportunities-and-build-resilience-for-displaced-rohingya-and-host-co","summary":"World Bank-backed support funded health, nutrition, education, water, shelters, livelihood support, and GBV prevention for Rohingya and host communities, with explicit attention to women and children. This is one of the clearest positive items for 6B.8, but it is externally financed and crisis-specific.","question_ids":["6B.8","6B.6","6B.7"]},{"title":"UNFPA Bangladesh Annual Report 2024","publisher":"UNFPA Bangladesh","date":"2024","url":"https://bangladesh.unfpa.org/en/unfpa-bangladesh-annual-report-2024","summary":"UNFPA reported targeted services for persons with disabilities, transgender people, sex workers, indigenous communities, adolescents, and disaster-affected women/girls, including dignity kits and emergency cash assistance. This is strong positive evidence for inclusive service delivery, though still mostly partner-led.","question_ids":["6B.8","6B.6","6B.7"]},{"title":"Freedom in the World 2024: Bangladesh","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/bangladesh/freedom-world/2024","summary":"Freedom House said Rohingya had limited access to health care, employment, and education; camp policies were punitive; minorities faced discrimination; and women were socially and politically disadvantaged. This directly cuts against equal opportunity and dignified inclusion.","question_ids":["6B.8","6B.7"]},{"title":"World Report 2024: Bangladesh","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/bangladesh","summary":"HRW reported abusive treatment of hijras, attacks on disability protesters, and severe restrictions on Rohingya access to education, movement, livelihoods, and basic assistance. This is strong evidence against a dignity-centered governing approach.","question_ids":["6B.8","6B.7"]},{"title":"Bangladesh: Türk decries government crackdown, urges respect for international human rights","publisher":"UN OHCHR","date":"July 26, 2024","url":"https://bangladesh.un.org/en/275065-bangladesh-t%C3%BCrk-decries-government-crackdown-urges-respect-international-human-rights","summary":"The UN said more than 170 people had been killed, some injured people were denied medical care, and internet shutdowns increased impunity; it also said there was no effort to protect people from attacks by government-affiliated groups. This is very strong negative evidence on dignity and civilian protection.","question_ids":["6B.8","6B.6"]},{"title":"Bangladesh: New Rohingya Refugees Lack Protection, Aid","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"September 25, 2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/25/bangladesh-new-rohingya-refugees-lack-protection-aid","summary":"HRW reported that some new Rohingya arrivals were denied health services because they lacked documentation, and that fear and camp violence made access to care and protection even harder. This is direct counterevidence to equal, dignified access.","question_ids":["6B.8","6B.6","6B.7"]},{"title":"Fears grip ethnic minorities after deadly violence in Bangladesh","publisher":"Reuters","date":"September 21, 2024","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/fears-grip-ethnic-minorities-after-deadly-violence-in-bangladesh-3626672","summary":"Reuters reported ethnic minorities in the Chittagong Hill Tracts living in fear after clashes, with homes and businesses burned and families displaced despite heavy patrols. That is direct evidence that poor regions and minorities were not securely protected.","question_ids":["6B.8","6B.6"]}]}
